item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1380

Stereo and views

  • A comp can have views: This comp > Views sets up left and right (or goes back to one). A .nk's views open and save back.
  • Every node works on each view. A mono branch gives the same picture to both.
  • Read: a file named with %V (the view's name) or %v (its first letter) reads one file a view; a stereo EXR reads with both views.
  • Write: an EXR holds every view (its views knob keeps some); other file types, or a name with %V or %v, write a file a view.
  • The Viewer has a menu for the view shown when the comp is stereo.
  • New nodes in Views: JoinViews, OneView, ShuffleViews, MixViews, SideBySide, Anaglyph and ReConverge.
  • Not yet: a knob with a different value in each view (a .nk's split knob opens with its first value, and the load report lists it).

New node

  • Dither (Filter): fine noise against banding before an 8- or 10-bit file, its own in each channel unless monodither, a new pattern each frame unless static seed.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1378

JPEG XL

  • Read opens JPEG XL (.jxl) stills, and the file browser lists them.
  • Write writes JPEG XL: give it a .jxl name or the jxl file type. Its own settings show for a .jxl: datatype (8 bit, 16 bit or 32 bit float), distance (0, the default, is lossless; 1 is visually lossless; higher makes smaller files) and effort (1 fastest to 9 smallest). Colour as a TIFF's for 8 and 16 bit, as an EXR's for float.

Faster

  • Nagi now also runs its temporal stage and its multiscale luma on the GPU: about three times faster than the last build at HD.
  • VectorGenerator is about 30% faster, Kronos and OFlow2 10 to 20% (the same pictures), EdgeExtend and Inpaint2 about 15%.

Fixes

  • Write's datatype now sets the bit depth of TIFF (8 bit, 16 bit, 32 bit float), PNG (8 or 16 bit) and DPX (8, 10, 12 or 16 bit) as well as EXR, so a Nuke script's 16-bit TIFF Write writes 16 bits.
  • A Radial's bounding box is now the area grown by a pixel (with its input's, unless replace is on), as in a Nuke script. A default Radial was its whole format, which made a Convolve with it slow.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1364

Camera tracking

  • CameraTracker tracks and solves: Track features finds corners and follows them, Solve makes the camera, Refine drops tracks over the error you set. Its panel shows the solve's error and a strip of it over the frames.
  • Its mask keeps features off moving things (the source's alpha, or a matte on the Mask input), and the film back comes from a camera menu or by hand. Keyframes are the solve's own choice or two frames you set.
  • In the Viewer: the tracks by state, the solved points reprojected, a readout over a track. Pick tracks, delete the picked ones, or pick every track over the error.
  • Export > Camera makes a Camera3 linked to the solve.

Help on the panel

  • A Help tab on the more involved nodes (the generative tools, Grain, Tracker, Roto and RotoPaint, Kento's own nodes): a short manual for that node, the same text as the Node Reference.

Viewer

  • Number keys over the Viewer switch which input it shows, instead of rewiring the graph, and the Viewer bar names the input shown.
  • Whole-number sliders now set their values; Cambi says what its score means.

Faster

  • On a Mac, the motion vectors under Kronos, OFlow2, VectorGenerator and MotionBlur are made on the GPU: about 1.8 times faster at HD, the same results.
  • Nagi runs its motion compensation and spatial stage on the GPU: about twice as fast.
  • ZDefocus2 is 13 times faster, Map Defocus 2.6 times with a map, Edge Wrap and Median nearly twice, and the expression-built nodes up to twice.
  • OpenFX plugins that render through Metal now do, a whole frame at a time.

Nodes

  • Nuke nodes our comps don't use and Kento won't build now are parked: they open, keep their settings and are written back, and say so.
